title: Perinatal care in Western Uganda: Prevalence and factors associated with appropriate care among women attending three district hospitals

false_alarm.note: The source states the stillbirth target as a global average of 8 per 1000 total births; 'less than 8' is a wording nuance of the same SDG/ENAP target, cited as part of a group [1-3].

Caused by the checker: the PDF splits the reference's DOI across a line break ('journal.pmed. 1002151'), the truncated DOI resolved to an unrelated tuberculosis review, and that wrong paper was flagged as off-topic. The real reference (Leslie et al., PLoS Med 2016) was never checked.

debatable.note: 64.1% and 24.7% do not appear in the cited Nepal study's text, but the checker's text of cited papers omits table contents, and the proportions may be in a table or derived from one.

The cited Ethiopian study says care quality 'might differ' with equipment, workload and provider commitment; the sentence's 'common occurrences in low income countries' is the citing authors' generalisation, cited jointly with [30].

Supply-chain strengthening is supported; the cited paper (northern Uganda scale-up) describes renovating specific operating theatres, not upgrading public and private facilities for clean and safe delivery in the region.

summary_line: Caught 3 of 3 planted errors · 2 false alarms
